## Block 15:46Z - B90 ORDER: choice + v4 built (n8n-flows-v4, film-v4, real-v4), test B90 added as NEW name; V7 commit 6ebb7f62e untouched

CHOICE: neither pure (a) option. The node timeout cannot be set below the claim window (Send Email node has NO timeout setting), and I have NO measured node timeout (AF2 not run). So: claim window 720 s (12 min), longer than the longest single wait I READ in the nodemailer code inside n8n 2.46.6 (connect 2 min, greeting 30 s, socket inactivity 10 min), PLUS a new node AlertBackoff on AlertSend's error output that resets the retry time to the old 60..300 s backoff, so a quick failure is not delayed to 12 min (AF1 behaviour kept). Why not only a longer claim: it would delay the retry after every quick failure. Cost: a hung SMTP can make the alert 12 to 13 min late; a send over 12 min or a failed mark can still duplicate.

Use lease 20 as before (--lease 20); MF_TRIES/MF_TMO_MS default.
(2) AF1: how the alert-only hold is made: the SMTP stand-in is given the file <mailfile>.rcptfail with text "2|alerts@example.test". At each RCPT TO the catcher reads it; if the recipient contains that text and the count is above 0 it decrements the count and answers "451 try later" (nothing stored); every other recipient (the intake address) is accepted as normal. So only alert sends fail, the lead mail is untouched. The lead mail itself is made "unknown" by .drop=1 (mail stored, acknowledgement dropped, as T12). It is NOT a time-based outage: "restored" means the two failures are used up (count 0), not that I switch something back.
Pass flag asserts ALL of: state reached unknown within 150 s; alerts 20 s after unknown = 0; at least 1 alert within 420 s; after a further 130 s exactly 1 alert for the lead; row state still unknown; mails to intake = 1 (the one stored before the dropped acknowledgement, no resend); CRM rows = 1; alert_sent = true in the table. It records alert_attempts and the leftover fault count. (Expected attempts 3.)
(3) SMTP dead for 10 minutes (BY DESIGN, not tested): alert_attempts has NO cap. Per lead the sweep retries at claim windows of 60, 120, 180, 240, 300 s, then every 300 s; the counter only counts. 10 minutes = about 4 to 5 attempts per lead. Who is told: nobody, until the SMTP works again: the only alert channel is the same SMTP/e-mail, so while it is dead there is NO notification and no second channel. That is a limit of this design, not solved; the unsent leads are visible in the table (state unknown/failed with alert_sent=false) to anyone who queries it. Can a dead SMTP spin the recovery: not by rate: at most 5 rows per tick and each row at most once per window, so a refused or fast-failing SMTP costs at most about 5 sends per 30 s. A HUNG SMTP (connection accepted, no answer; the node has no timeout setting, transport timeout is the library default which I have not measured) is the open risk: each 30 s tick starts its own recovery execution, a hung send keeps that execution alive, executions can pile up one per tick until the transport timeout frees them. Lease recovery (ClaimStuck) runs before the alert branch in the same tick, so it is not blocked by its own tick's alert, but I have NOT tested pile-up or its memory/connection cost. A spec for that test (hold the greeting with .pre for 10 minutes, count open recovery executions and SMTP connections) is not written yet.

F-c (SMTP delay past node timeout -> state unknown, 0 alerts). Where the alert comes from, in mf-sub-crm-mail: two places only. (A) SendMail error output -> MarkUnknownA (sets unknown, only if claim_token still matches) -> UnknownNewA -> AlertUnknown. (B) a recovery re-run: MailClaim finds mail_sent already true -> empty -> MarkUnknownB (mail_sent and token match) -> UnknownNew -> AlertUnknown. SendMail has retry off and no timeout setting (n8n SMTP node), so "past node timeout" means the transport's own timeout (not set by me).
Hole by reading (not reproduced): AlertUnknown is itself an SMTP send with onError continueRegularOutput, and the state is already unknown, which recovery never touches again (ClaimStuck excludes unknown). If that alert send fails or hangs (same SMTP server, same delay), the error is swallowed and NOTHING retries: state unknown, 0 alerts = exactly lane3's F-c. The same hole exists for AlertFailed in mf-recovery (state failed is set first, then the send, continueRegularOutput, no retry). It would hit when the delay is a before-greeting hold (.pre style: the alert connection is held too) or any persistent SMTP fault; a delay that comes AFTER the catcher stores the mail would still count as an alert in alerts(), so lane3's mode matters. Please send me: which SMTP fault mode lane3 used (.pre or .delay or drop), whether it was still on when the alert was sent, and the node error text in the log if any.
Second, smaller point: if mail_sent is true and attempts reach 3, MarkFailed sets failed (not unknown) and AlertFailed's text says failed; the lead gets an alert but the wording is wrong. Not lost.
Proposed fix (NOT pushed, needs your go because it changes the "exactly 1 alert" test count to "at least 1, duplicates possible only if the send succeeded but the mark failed"): add column alerted boolean default false; after each alert node set alerted=true where lead_key and state in (unknown, failed); recovery gets a third branch every 30 s: SELECT leads in unknown/failed with alerted=false, send alert (text by state), then set alerted=true; alert nodes with retry 3 times. Effect: an alert lost to an SMTP fault is retried until SMTP works; cost: one more recovery branch and SQL column. Tests to add: T16 = SMTP held (.pre 60 s) during the unknown case: expect state unknown, alert arrives after the hold is removed, at least 1 and at most 2 alerts.
